description:
Found s395 the moment the @{+} fold let re/pat_rt_report.t run (#314 single).
The file reaches line 343,

    $_ = "x"; /x(?{func "in regexp"})/;

and dies with

    sb-kernel::control-stack-exhausted: Control stack exhausted

which truncates the last ~82 of its 2513 rows (it stops at 2431 ok / 39 not-ok).

`(?{ CODE })` / `(??{ CODE })` are a DELIBERATE non-support -- they have their
own docs/not-supported.md section.  The bug is not that they do not work, it
is HOW they do not work: rule 12's boundary (docs/fable-answers-s328.md §1)
says an unsupported construct announces or dies NAMING ITSELF; a stack
exhaustion names nothing, and it takes the rest of the file with it.  A clean
per-match refusal would leave every later assertion running.

DIAGNOSE FIRST (do not assume): the exhaustion may be in the pattern
TRANSLATION (a code block re-entering the pattern compiler) or in cl-ppcre.
The cheap discriminating measurement is to compile the pattern alone under
sbcl and see which stack it blows:

    echo '$_ = "x"; /x(?{ 1 })/; print "survived\n";' | ./runpcl

BAR: the construct announces itself once (or dies naming the pattern), the
file runs to its end, and the not-supported entry gains the measured row
count.  Re-run re/pat_rt_report.t and splice its snapshot row (expect ~2513
rows attempted rather than 2431).


PROBES ALREADY RUN s395 (do NOT repeat -- none reproduce):
  * `$_ = "x"; /x(?{ 1 })/;`                       survives (block simply does not run)
  * the whole func/standalone/subst/multiline-subst/(?{func}) block, standalone: survives;
    the (?{ }) call is silently skipped, the other three run
  * `split /(?{ split "" })/, "abc"` (line 328, nested split): survives, gives a-b-c
  * the study + `push @x, $& while m/.../gx` block (line 331): survives
So the exhaustion is NOT any one of those statements read alone -- it needs
the file`s accumulated state (2431 assertions of it).  Next step: bisect by
running the file with a truncation point, or raise SBCL`s control stack and
see what the deep frame actually is.

=== DIAGNOSED AND FIXED s399 — IT WAS THE HARNESS, NOT `(?{ CODE })` ===

The s395 probes were right that no statement in the file reproduces the
exhaustion, and right to suspect accumulated state.  Both were the wrong
track: **`tools/run-perl-suite.pl` was the only runner that did not pass
`--control-stack-size 512`**, so the companion suite ran PCL on SBCL's 2 MB
default — a control stack 256x smaller than every other measurement in the
project uses:

    Pl/t/PCLCore.pm        --control-stack-size 512   (the gate)
    sweep-perl-tests.pl    --control-stack-size 512
    ./runpcl               --control-stack-size 512
    tools/run-perl-suite.pl   (nothing)               <- the bug

That is why the probes "did not reproduce": they were run through ./runpcl,
which has the flag.  The discriminating measurement was to run the SAME
transpiled file under the SAME sbcl invocation the suite uses, and it took
one line to see.

FIXED s399 by adding the flag to both branches of the runner's $sbcl
(core and source mode), ordered as Pl/t/PCLCore.pm already orders it.

MEASURED — all four files the snapshot recorded as control-stack-exhausted:

    re/pat_rt_report.t   2431 ok / 39  CRASH  ->  2454 ok / 56, runs to the end
    op/utf8cache.t          0 ok /  2  CRASH  ->     2 ok /  0
    re/pat_psycho.t         0 ok / 11  CRASH  ->    11 ok /  0   (now SLOW)
    re/speed.t              0 ok /  0  CRASH  ->     1 ok /  0   (now SLOW)

so +37 C_ok and four crashes gone.  The two "now SLOW" files are the real
residue: with the bigger stack they no longer die early, they RUN the
pathological patterns they exist to time, and PCL's cl-ppcre is slow on them
(re/pat_psycho.t needs > 400 s under --jobs 1; re/speed.t produced 1 of
perl's 59 rows at 300 s).  That is a SPEED fact about PCL, not a crash, and
it is the honest state.

WHAT REMAINS OF THE ORIGINAL TASK: nothing about `(?{ CODE })`.  The
construct is still a deliberate non-support with its own not-supported
section, and the file's snapshot row must lose the "(?{ CODE }) regex code
block, task #324" attribution -- it was never the cause.  If a future
session wants the two slow files measured, the mechanism is
docs/perl-suite-timeouts.tsv (effective timeout = max(row, --timeout)) and
the cost is minutes of every full companion run for ~12 rows; decide that
deliberately.

LESSON (worth generalising): when ONE runner disagrees with the others about
a crash, diff the RUNNERS before diffing the code.  Every runner in this
project spawns sbcl with its own hand-written option string, and this is the
second time one of them has drifted (the first: the sweep's `--load` of the
test library).  A shared helper that builds the sbcl command line for all
four would have made this impossible.

COST OF THE FLAG, measured s399 (know this before raising --jobs): the runner
spawns a PERL side and a PCL side per worker, so `--jobs 8` now reserves 8 x
512 MB of control stack at once.  A `--all --jobs 8 --timeout 300` run was
SIGTERMed by the machine's memory guard after 41 of 521 files ("RUN DID NOT
COMPLETE — most likely out of memory", the runner's own message).  `--jobs 4`
runs comfortably (MemAvailable stayed above 10 GB), and the project's own
snapshot practice was already `--jobs 6` (s392).  The size is overridable —
`PCL_SUITE_STACK_MB=64 tools/run-perl-suite.pl …` — so a smaller stack is one
env var away if a machine needs it; 512 is what every other runner uses and
what the four files above were verified at.


DONE s400 (13b6e1a): verification finished.  The last 135 files (re/, run/,
uni/) run with the flag — 125 identical to the snapshot, 9 TIMEOUT-shaped
(not comparable), 1 mover (re/pat_advanced.t), and the mover is NOT the flag:
same numbers at PCL_SUITE_STACK_MB=2, emitted CL byte-identical, bisect lands
on #323.  The re/pat_psycho.t + re/speed.t timeouts.tsv decision is still
open and is now part of the #345 portfolio question.
subject: (?{ CODE }) was NOT the cause: tools/run-perl-suite.pl was the only runner without --control-stack-size, so the companion suite ran PCL on a 2 MB stack (FIXED s399, +37 C_ok over four files)
